results.snippet:
# Enforcement

If you violate any of our Platform Terms or Developer Policies your app and possibly your account will be enforced upon. Enforcement actions for violations will vary. When enforcing on an app, we consider the severity and nature of the violation, the developer’s policy compliance history, and the violation’s impact on users. Enforcement actions for policy violations may include (but are not limited to) any of the following:

- a warning
- restricting the app's ability to perform certain actions for a period of time (e.g., posting content)
- revocation of approved permissions and features
- deactivation and removal of the application
- deactivation and deletion of developer account

Please note, you will still be able to test login for apps that have been restricted. Find more information on app role testing here.

## Violation Details

The developer appeals page lists all of your apps that have been enforced on and the Terms and Policies they have violated.

## Violation Notifications

We will communicate information about policy violations through developer notifications and emails.

### Email

Enforcement emails are sent to the email address listed in each app’s Contact Email field in the Settings > Basic panel in the App Dashboard.

results.title: Developer account suspended under Platform Term 7.e.i.2: requesting a review - Developer Community Forum - Meta for Developers
results.snippet:
Hi, our developer account was suspended and I would like to request a review, as I believe this may be an automated enforcement error.

Enforcement message received: "Platform Term 7.e.i.2 - Negative impact on the platform, products, data or users. We determined that your app is negatively affecting the platform, products, data or users and violated or may have violated our terms."

What our app does (legitimate use): It is an internal reporting dashboard for our marketing agency. It uses the Marketing API in read-only mode to pull performance metrics (spend, impressions, clicks, conversions) from our own and our managed clients' ad accounts, so we can generate reports. We do not resell data, we do not scrape user data, and we perform no write actions on user content.

Why I believe this is a false positive: We are a small operation with a limited number of ad accounts and low API volume, using standard Marketing API endpoints (insights, customconversions, adaccounts). The notice itself says we "may have violated," which points to an automated flag rather than a confirmed violation.

What I have already done: I submitted an appeal through the App Dashboard on July 25, 2026 and I am still waiting for a response.
